# Introduction

Quarto documents are very similar to Rmd documents. The advantage is that you get two editors that you can switch between in the toggle top left (Source vs. Visual). It can be convenient to use the Visual one, for example when 'hand-writing' a table. You can also access other formatting help in the task bar above.

Referencing literature works the same as in Rmd (brackets and at), for example [@Gao2026] .

| Abbreviation | Description         |
|--------------|---------------------|
| Rmd          | R-markdown document |
| Qmd          | Quarto document     |

: Table that has quickly been added using the "Table" toggle in the task bar

In this document, we also use the new trcpetc workflow for tables, i.e. table_one() to get the raw descriptives, then kable_table_one to automatically make the header nice etc.

## Statistical analysis

Clinical characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. Continuous variables were characterized using median and interquartile range; dichotomous or polytomous variables were characterized using frequencies.

Between-group comparisons were evaluated using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for continuous variables and Fisher's exact tests for dichotomous and polytomous variables.

Time to death was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods, and administratively censored at XX years.

Time to first reintervention was analyzed using a competing-risks framework, 
with death  treated as a competing event, with administrative censoring at XX years. 
Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) for reintervention were estimated according to GROUP. 
The cumulative incidence functions were compared using Gray's test.

Serial XXX measurements were evaluated longitudinally. Repeated measurements within patients were 
accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEE), with GROUP, time, and their 
interaction as fixed effects and patient identifier as the clustering variable. An exchangeable 
working correlation structure was used. The interaction between GROUP and time was used to assess
whether the trajectories differed between the groups, and expressed as p-value. Individual patient 
trajectories are shown with locally estimated scatterplot smoothing (LOESS) curves for each group.

Analyses were performed using `r R.version.string` (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria).

## Survial and competing risk figures added as tabsets as an example

::: panel-tabset

### Overall survival

```{r tab-surv, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| tbl-cap: "Survival summary by group"

km %>% summarize_km(time_lab = 'Months since surgery')
```

```{r fig-surv, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Kaplan-Meier curve with log-rank test"

km %>%
    show_surv(x_lab = "Months since surgery", pvalue_pos = "bottomright", atrisk_init_pos = -0.15,
    x_lim = c(0,24), x_break = c(0,6, 12, 18, 24)) # Use up to the time you admin-censored!
```

### Time-to-any reintervention (competing risk example)

```{r tab-anyre, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| tbl-cap: "Cumulative incidence of any reintervention."

cif %>% summarize_cif(time_lab = 'Years since surgery', evt_type= 1, x_lim = c(0,24), x_break = c(0,6, 12, 18, 24))

```

```{r fig-anyre, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative incidence functions for any reintervention, with death treated as a competing event. Follow-up was administratively censored at XX years. P value from Gray's test."

cif %>%
    show_cif(evt_type = 1,
             y_lab = 'Proportion of patients with any reintervention',
             x_lab = 'Years since surgery'
             )


```
